messages:
Maya: Quick loop — thinking out loud about adding a per-request ‘microprofile’ that pins quantization/window hints (FP8/INT8/4bit) for the runtime. This would let customers opt into a tuned lane without changing endpoint-level profiles.@Liam any concerns about API surface?
Liam: I like the idea. Main risk is explosion of combos at the runtime dispatch layer. Need to define a tiny contract: which fields are allowed, what’s advisory vs authoritative.
Neha: +1. Also need to be explicit about quality SLAs. If a microprofile requests FP8 but model/host doesn't support it, do we fallback automatically? What telemetry do we emit?
Maya: Proposal: microprofile = {"precision_hint":"fp8|int8|4bit","calib_tier":"conservative|balanced|aggressive","kv_cache_scope":"pin|shared"}. Runtime treats precision_hint as advisory; operator policy can enforce. If unsupported, fallback to next-safe precision and emit a structured event.
Sam: Sounds ok. How do we surface "next-safe"? Is it ordered by cost (4bit->int8->fp8) or quality? We need deterministic rules.
Jules: Suggestion: order by measured quality delta for the model family (we have matrices for that). Default fallback order = quality-preserving then cost-preserving. Ops can override per-customer.
Liam: Implementation concern: dispatch table keys may need to include microprofile fingerprint — could blow up GPU pool partitioning. Maybe we canonicalize microprofiles into a small set of runtime lanes (N buckets) at admission time.
Neha: For telemetry, we should emit: microprofile.requested, microprofile.applied, microprofile.fallback_reason, quality_regression_score (if available), and latency_delta. Keep events small.
Maya: Agreed. Can we reuse existing precision-profile IDs (the quant profiles) and allow microprofiles to reference them by affinity instead of full spec? That reduces cardinality.
Sam: That helps. But still need a short-lived mapping step: microprofile -> canonical_profile_id. That mapping should be cacheable and versioned. Add TTL and an ops endpoint to invalidate.
Jules: Operational safety note: when a canonical profile changes, we must not silently switch in-flight requests. Version the profiles and include profile_version in telemetry.
Liam: Rollout plan: start with a shadow phase where microprofiles are accepted but only logged; then a canary that actually activates for 1% traffic on noncritical endpoints; finally gated enable by endpoint.
Maya: I'll draft a short RFC with the contract, examples, and a toy admission algorithm. Action items: Maya write RFC, Neha list telemetry fields + schema, Liam prototype canonicalization cache, Sam ops invalidation endpoint.
deploy-bot: Canary deployment queued: precision-adm-service v0.3 -> staging.
Maya: Thanks — will ping when RFC is up. :thumbsup:
